title: Russian Espionage Group Exploited Zimbra Zero-Day to Steal Mail and 2FA Codes
summary: A Russian state-supported espionage group spent months reading Western mailboxes through a then-unknown flaw in Zimbra's webmail client.
card_summary: A Russian state-supported espionage group spent months reading Western mailboxes through a then-unknown flaw in Zimbra's webmail client.

sections.impact:
The payload goes after the last 90 days of email, the organization's entire email directory, the password saved in the browser and the codes kept for two-factor recovery.

Assessed severity: CRITICAL.
sections.context: This story is part of the recurring zero-day pattern where exploitation pressure is highest before broad patch adoption.
